The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 yesterday in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals.
Jordan Carnes reports from member station KALW.
Saturday's game marked the Valkyries' first appearance in the Finals, while the Dream's last visit was in 2013.
Both teams surprised the league with dominant playoff runs.
Each sweeping the former consecutive champs, the Aces and the Liberty in the semifinals.
Game 1 was marked by defense.
The Valkyries are the top-ranked defensive team in the league, while the Dream's Angel Reiss was named Defensive Player of the Year.
However, it wasn't enough to beat the Valkyries on their home turf, Ball Hala, which has sold out every game in its two years.
Game 2 of the Best of Seven series will be on Monday in San Francisco.
For NPR News, I'm Jordan Carnes.
A new environmental study finds President Trump's plan to paint the Eisenhower Executive Office building next to the White House would diminish the historic character and the original design of the building.
The president has suggested painting the 19th-century historic landmark, calling the gray exterior, in his words, "a really bad color."
The study finds the project would cost at least $7.5 million.
It also states the granite is not meant to be painted, and that doing so would trap moisture and degrade the stone.
Trump has been looking at painting the building as part of his push to remake the nation's capital, which so far has included the White House Ballroom, the Reflecting Pool, and the Triumphal Arch.
I'm Lyndy Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
